title: STPI Inaugurates its 75th Centre in Bareilly to Strengthen Uttar Pradesh’s IT/ITeS and Startup Ecosystem
subtitle:
New Centre to Strengthen Technology Infrastructure and Support IT/ITeS Enterprises, Startups and Technology-led Entrepreneurship in the Rohilkhand Region
Initiative Aims to Promote Innovation, Facilitate Business Opportunities and Encourage Employment Generation in the Region
body_text: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, inaugurated its Bareilly Centre in Uttar Pradesh. The centre was inaugurated by Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, and Commerce & Industry, Government of India , in the presence of Dr. Arun Kumar Saxena, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Forest & Environment, Zoological Garden and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh; Shri Chhatrapal Singh Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Bareilly and Smt. Shruti Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI among other dignitaries. The inauguration marks an important milestone for STPI as Bareilly becomes its 75 th centre in the country, further expanding its nationwide network and commitment to strengthening India's technology ecosystem beyond established metropolitan hubs. Of STPI's 75 centres, 67 are located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities , reflecting its sustained focus on decentralising technology infrastructure and enabling regional entrepreneurship. Developed with an investment of approximately ₹18.25 crore on a 2-acre land parcel, the Bareilly Centre will strengthen the regional IT/ITeS ecosystem by providing an institutional platform for technology enterprises and emerging entrepreneurs. Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, and Commerce & Industry, Government of India, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly centre is a landmark gift not only for Bareilly, but for the youth of the entire Rohilkhand region especially Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, and Badaun so they no longer have to migrate to major hubs like Mumbai, Noida, and Hyderabad for IT, startups, incubation, innovation, and research, instead gaining world-class technical facilities right at home while shaping the future of coming generations and driving local job creation. Under the visionary leadership and long-term policies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, just as center-state coordination drives growth, trade and technology serve as twin engines of India's progress, while commitments to train one crore youth in artificial intelligence (AI), build a semiconductor chip manufacturing and packaging ecosystem to reduce foreign dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience after disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic, expand data centers and software exports, and advance Atmanirbhar Bharat are accelerating India's technological self-reliance and creating new opportunities for young people." "In the IT sector, India stands today as the world's Talent Capital, powered by youth technical skill and design capabilities, and providing free technical facilities through STPI alongside skill development and support ensures that financial constraints never hold back talent and enterprise. As local MSMEs, IT industries, chambers of commerce, and entrepreneurs utilize the center to full capacity, we will expand additional buildings and technical facilities, while Common Service Centers (CSCs) under Digital India continue expanding rural access to Aadhaar, banking, electricity bill payments, and citizen services—giving me complete confidence, alongside commendations to STPI Director General Arvind Kumar and his team, that like Noida, Kanpur, Lucknow, and Gorakhpur, Bareilly will emerge as a major IT hub propelling technical and economic growth across Rohilkhand.” Dr. Arun Kumar Saxena, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Forest & Environment, Zoological Garden and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh, said, “The establishment of the STPI Bareilly Centre is a welcome development for the region and will contribute to expanding opportunities in the technology sector. Bareilly and the surrounding areas have considerable potential in terms of talent and entrepreneurship. The centre will provide an important platform for young people, startups and technology enterprises to explore new opportunities, develop innovative ideas and contribute to the state's economic progress.” Shri Chhatrapal Singh Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Bareilly, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly Centre is a significant milestone for the region. It will help create a stronger foundation for technology-led entrepreneurship and provide aspiring entrepreneurs and young professionals with access to a wider ecosystem of opportunities. Smt. Shruti Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly Centre is an encouraging development for the region, particularly for its young talent and aspiring entrepreneurs. Access to technology infrastructure and a supportive startup ecosystem can help unlock local potential, encourage innovative thinking and create new avenues for professional growth. ” Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, said, “The inauguration of the Bareilly Centre marks a significant milestone in STPI's journey, taking our nationwide network to 75 centres, of which 67 are located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. This reflects our continued commitment to extending technology infrastructure and entrepreneurial opportunities beyond established IT hubs and enabling emerging regions to participate in India's digital economy. Developed with an investment of approximately ₹18.25 crore on a 2-acre land parcel, the Bareilly Centre is an important addition to this network and will provide an enabling environment for IT/ITeS enterprises, startups and aspiring entrepreneurs in the Rohilkhand region. Through our infrastructure, incubation initiatives and industry linkages, we aim to nurture local talent, facilitate business growth and support the development of innovative technology-led enterprises.” The Bareilly Centre further expands STPI's nationwide presence and its efforts to promote the IT/ITeS industry beyond established technology hubs. Through its network of centres, incubation facilities and entrepreneurship initiatives, STPI continues to support startups and technology enterprises through infrastructure, industry linkages and opportunities for product development and intellectual property creation. The event was also attended by several prominent dignitaries and public representatives . The inauguration marks an important step towards strengthening Uttar Pradesh's regional technology ecosystem, encouraging entrepreneurship and enabling technology-led economic growth through greater collaboration among government, industry, academia and startups. About STPI: Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), engaged in promoting the IT/ITES industry, innovation, research and development, startups, and product and intellectual property creation in emerging technology domains. These include the Internet of Things, blockchain, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, augmented and virtual reality, animation and visual effects, and data science and analytics. STPI supports innovation across domains such as gaming, fintech, agritech, medtech, autonomous and connected mobility, ESDM, cybersecurity, Industry 4.0 and drones. **** Kanishk Sharma / Vinod Kumar
